outlook.statement: Cautiously optimistic about prospects for the textile industry and the Company; expects improved business momentum across domestic and export markets as global uncertainties subside and demand conditions normalise
Easing of geopolitical disruptions, moderation in tariff-related uncertainties and improving stability in raw material prices expected to create more predictable operating environment
Low inventory levels across textile value chain; any sustained improvement in market conditions expected to trigger inventory replenishment creating meaningful demand momentum
Government's announcement of ECLGS 5.0 expected to provide timely support for industry working capital requirements, improving liquidity across sector

The Company aims to strengthen the proportion of value-added products without compromising operational flexibility or customer responsiveness. Focus on strengthening presence across domestic and international markets through value-added products, customer diversification, and geographic growth.

Global supply chain reconfiguration is creating a generational opportunity for Indian textile manufacturers. India is emerging as a credible alternative sourcing destination, particularly for value-added and specialised products.

The textile industry appears to be emerging from an extended cyclical downtrend. Yarn realisations began strengthening by approximately Rs 10-15 per Kg in Q1 2025-26, with restocking cycle benefiting focused value-added producers.

The global textile market is projected to increase from USD 660.13 billion in 2025 to USD 702.97 billion in 2026 (CAGR 6.5%), reaching approximately USD 919.08 billion by 2030 at a CAGR of 6.9%. The Indian textile and apparel market was valued at USD 248.70 billion in 2025 and is expected to reach USD 656.31 billion by 2034, expanding at a CAGR of 11.38% during 2026–2034. India targets textile and apparel exports of USD 100 billion by 2030 through greater market access, product diversification and proposed FTAs with EU, UK and Canada. Domestic market targeting USD 250 billion by 2030. The World Bank revised FY27 growth estimate upward to approximately 6.6%, with India expected to retain its position as the fastest-growing major economy.

Indian technical textiles market projected to reach nearly USD 60.4 billion by 2030, highlighting growing strategic importance in high-value applications such as healthcare, mobility, infrastructure and defence.
Ongoing free trade agreement discussions with major economies such as the UK and EU are expected to create new opportunities for India's textile and apparel exports in global markets.
The Company is exploring options for increasing the renewable energy capacity going forward.

The Indian textile market is gaining momentum and is set for resurgence on account of strong growth in the domestic and export markets. The Company intends to leverage this along with its long-standing customer relations, deep focus on understanding its customer's needs, excellent post-sales service, innovative product development and versatile product mix to further strengthen its sales both globally and in the domestic market. Furthermore, the company has actively taken steps to enhance economies of scale, increase productivity, reduce costs, shrink delivery schedules, invest in the research and development of new products and aggressively pursue opportunities in new markets. The Company is also evaluating the feasibility of a diversification and expansion project which will further improve the Company's bottom line.
Due to the modernization of the old ring frame and continuing focus on value-added products, consistent quality and versatile product mix, we expect better performance in the upcoming years.
